faqs.q: What can go wrong with my sewer lines?
faqs.a: Everything that goes into our sink, shower and tub drains, our toilets and our garbage disposals finds its way to the sewer line: hair, shampoo, soap, toothpaste, cooking grease, chicken bones, pasta and rice. Since the first rule of plumbing is that water heads downhill, it is not surprising that drain and sewer lines become clogged.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to replace a sewer line?
faqs.a: Every job is different and the cost depends on the length of the line and how much of it needs replacing. For the replacement alone, expect somewhere between $55 and $95 per foot of installed pipe. For a complete house-to-street replacement, the average homeowner is looking at $4,000 up to $25,000 and beyond, once excavation, landscaping and backfilling are counted.

faqs.q: Does homeowner's insurance cover sewer line repair or replacement?
faqs.a: Standard homeowner's policies rarely, if ever, include repair or replacement of sewer lines. Secondary policies covering sewer line expenses are available from a number of companies at around $20 a month for $5,000 a year of benefits. Read the fine print, as some customers report excavation and pavement restoration costs they still had to pay out of pocket.

faqs.q: What if my sewer line is beneath a slab?
faqs.a: More and more Houston homes sit on concrete slabs, and much of the water supply and drain pipework runs beneath them. A leak under the slab shifts a lot of soil and can move the foundation with it. Cracked patios, doors that are hard to open and close, cracks in the drywall and sloped or squeaky floorboards are all signs of water leaking beneath a slab, and it needs correcting quickly to prevent foundation damage. Reaching those lines takes some excavation, though the cured-in-place pipe method is now an alternative to digging the slab up.

faqs.q: What is trenchless sewer line repair?
faqs.a: The cured-in-place pipe method uses a felt tube soaked in epoxy that runs the length of your original sewer line. Once it is snaked into place, hot air expands it to fit the pipe walls and speeds the curing, and the result is a new lining that will last for decades without massive excavation.

A sewer belly occurs when the soil beneath the sewer line erodes or washes away. The unsupported section sags, creating low spots where wastewater and sediment collect, and bellied pipes are more likely to leak because the movement creates stress cracks between pipe segments. A bellied line needs to be repaired or replaced by a licensed plumbing technician.

faqs.q: How much do AC services cost in Houston?
faqs.a: It depends on the service, the complexity and the system, but on average AC repairs run $150 to $600 and up, a new AC installation $4,500 to $9,000 depending on unit size and efficiency, maintenance visits $100 to $200 per tune-up, and a mini-split installation $3,000 to $8,000 per system. Pricing is given upfront and financing is available.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my air conditioner?
faqs.a: Watch for frequent breakdowns and recurring repairs, high energy bills despite normal usage, uneven cooling or weak airflow, strange noises such as banging, squealing or grinding, and a unit over 10 to 15 years old. If you are unsure, Nick's will give you an honest evaluation.
